nips.title: Basic protocol flow description
nips.summary: This NIP defines the basic protocol that should be implemented by everybody. New NIPs may add new optional (or mandatory) fields and messages and features to the structures and flows described here.

nips.title: Follow List
nips.summary: A special event with kind 3, meaning "follow list" is defined as having a list of p tags, one for each of the followed/known profiles one is following.

nips.title: OpenTimestamps Attestations for Events
nips.summary: This NIP defines an event with kind:1040 that can contain an OpenTimestamps proof for any other event:

unrecommended.reason: vulnerable to one specific attack, needs update

nips.title: Encrypted Direct Message
nips.summary: A special event with kind 4, meaning "encrypted direct message". It is supposed to have the following attributes:

nips.title: Mapping Nostr keys to DNS-based internet identifiers
nips.summary: On events of kind 0 (user metadata) one can specify the key "nip05" with an internet identifier (an email-like address) as the value. Although there is a link to a very liberal "internet identifier" specification above, the <local-part> part MUST only use characters a-z0-9-_..
headings: Finding users from their NIP-05 identifier
Clients must always follow public keys, not NIP-05 addresses
Public keys must be in hex format
Showing just the domain as an identifier

nips.title: Basic key derivation from mnemonic seed phrase
nips.summary: BIP39 is used to generate mnemonic seed words and derive a binary seed from them.

nips.title: window.nostr capability for web browsers
nips.summary: The window.nostr object may be made available by web browsers or extensions and websites or web-apps may make use of it after checking its availability.

nips.title: Handling Mentions
nips.summary: This document standardizes the treatment given by clients of inline mentions of other events and pubkeys inside the content of text_notes.

nips.title: Event Deletion Request
nips.summary: A special event with kind 5, meaning "deletion request" is defined as having a list of one or more e or a tags, each referencing an event the author is requesting to be deleted. Deletion requests SHOULD include a k tag for the kind of each event being requested for deletion.
headings: Deletion Request of a Deletion Request

nips.title: Text Notes and Threads
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:1 as a simple plaintext note.

nips.title: Relay Information Document
nips.summary: Relays may provide server metadata to clients to inform them of capabilities, administrative contacts, and various server attributes. This is made available as a JSON document over HTTP, on the same URI as the relay's websocket.

nips.title: Generic Tag Queries
nips.summary: Moved to NIP-01.

nips.title: Proof of Work
nips.summary: This NIP defines a way to generate and interpret Proof of Work for nostr notes. Proof of Work (PoW) is a way to add a proof of computational work to a note. This is a bearer proof that all relays and clients can universally validate with a small amount of code. This proof can be used as a means of spam deterrence.

nips.title: Subject tag in text events
nips.summary: This NIP defines the use of the "subject" tag in text (kind: 1) events. (implemented in more-speech)

nips.title: Nostr Marketplace (for resilient marketplaces)
nips.summary: Implemented in NostrMarket and Plebeian Market.
headings: Event 30017: Create or update a stall.
Event 30018: Create or update a product
Event 30019: Create or update marketplace UI/UX
Event 30020: Create or update a product sold as an auction

nips.title: Event Treatment
nips.summary: Moved to NIP-01.

nips.title: Private Direct Messages
nips.summary: This NIP defines an encrypted chat scheme which uses NIP-44 encryption and NIP-59 gift-wrapping.

nips.title: Reposts
nips.summary: A repost is a kind 6 event that is used to signal to followers that a kind 1 text note is worth reading.

nips.title: bech32-encoded entities
nips.summary: This NIP standardizes bech32-formatted strings that can be used to display keys, ids and other information in clients. These formats are not meant to be used anywhere in the core protocol, they are only meant for displaying to users, copy-pasting, sharing, rendering QR codes and inputting data.

nips.title: Command Results
nips.summary: Moved to NIP-01.

nips.title: nostr: URI scheme
nips.summary: This NIP standardizes the usage of a common URI scheme for maximum interoperability and openness in the network.
headings: Linking HTML pages to Nostr entities

nips.title: Comment
nips.summary: A comment is a threading note always scoped to a root event or an I-tag.

nips.title: Long-form Content
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:30023 (an addressable event) for long-form text content, generally referred to as "articles" or "blog posts".

nips.title: Extra metadata fields and tags
nips.summary: This NIP keeps track of extra optional fields that can added to events which are not defined anywhere else but have become de facto standards and other minor implementation possibilities that do not deserve their own NIP and do not have a place in other NIPs.

nips.title: Reactions
nips.summary: A reaction is a kind 7 event that is used to indicate user reactions to other events. A reaction's content field MUST include user-generated-content indicating the value of the reaction (conventionally +, -, or an emoji).

nips.title: Delegated Event Signing
nips.summary: This NIP defines how events can be delegated so that they can be signed by other keypairs.

unrecommended.reason: adds unnecessary burden for little gain

nips.title: Text Note References
nips.summary: This document standardizes the treatment given by clients of inline references of other events and profiles inside the .content of any event that has readable text in its .content (such as kinds 1 and 30023).
headings: Example of a profile mention process

nips.title: Public Chat
nips.summary: This NIP defines new event kinds for public chat channels, channel messages, and basic client-side moderation.

nips.title: Relay-based Groups
nips.summary: This NIP defines a standard for groups that are only writable by a closed set of users. They can be public for reading by external users or not.
headings: Moving a group to another relay
Checking your own membership in a group

nips.title: Custom Emoji
nips.summary: Custom emoji may be added to kind 0, kind 1, kind 1111 (NIP-22), kind 7 (NIP-25) and kind 30315 (NIP-38) events by including one or more "emoji" tags, in the form:

nips.title: Dealing with Unknown Events
nips.summary: When creating a new custom event kind that is part of a custom protocol and isn't meant to be read as text (like kind:1), clients should use an alt tag to write a short human-readable plaintext summary of what that event is about.

nips.title: Labeling
nips.summary: This NIP defines two new indexable tags to label events and a new event kind (kind:1985) to attach those labels to existing events. This supports several use cases, including distributed moderation, collection management, license assignment, and content classification.

nips.title: Parameterized Replaceable Events
nips.summary: Renamed to "Addressable events" and moved to NIP-01.

nips.title: git stuff
nips.summary: This NIP defines all the ways code collaboration using and adjacent to git can be done using Nostr.
headings: Possible things to be added later

nips.title: Torrents
nips.summary: This NIP defined a new kind 2003 which is a Torrent.

nips.title: Sensitive Content
nips.summary: The content-warning tag enables users to specify if the event's content needs to be approved by readers to be shown. Clients can hide the content until the user acts on it.

nips.title: Draft Events
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind 31234 as an encrypted storage for unsigned draft events of any other kind.

nips.title: User Statuses
nips.summary: This NIP enables a way for users to share live statuses such as what music they are listening to, as well as what they are currently doing: work, play, out of office, etc.

nips.title: Linking Profiles to Other Platforms
nips.summary: Users can declare their control over one or more online identities such as usernames, profile pages, keypairs in kind 10011 using i tags.

nips.title: Expiration Timestamp
nips.summary: The expiration tag enables users to specify a unix timestamp at which the message SHOULD be considered expired (by relays and clients) and SHOULD be deleted by relays.

nips.title: Authentication of clients to relays
nips.summary: This NIP defines a way for clients to authenticate to relays by signing an ephemeral event.
headings: auth-required in response to a REQ message
auth-required in response to an EVENT message

nips.title: Relay Access Metadata and Requests
nips.summary: This NIP defines a way for relays to advertise membership lists, and for clients to request admission to relays on behalf of users.

nips.title: Encrypted Payloads (Versioned)
nips.summary: The NIP introduces a new data format for keypair-based encryption. This NIP is versioned to allow multiple algorithm choices to exist simultaneously. This format may be used for many things, but MUST be used in the context of a signed event as described in NIP-01.

nips.title: Counting results
nips.summary: Relays may support the verb COUNT, which provides a mechanism for obtaining event counts.

messages.description: used to send requested event counts to clients

nips.title: Nostr Remote Signing
nips.summary: Private keys should be exposed to as few systems - apps, operating systems, devices - as possible as each system adds to the attack surface.
headings: Direct connection initiated by the client
Example flow for signing an event
Example event signing request with auth challenge

nips.title: Nostr Wallet Connect
nips.summary: This NIP describes a way for clients to access a remote lightning wallet through a standardized protocol. Custodians may implement this, or the user may run a bridge that bridges their wallet/node and the Nostr Wallet Connect protocol.

nips.title: Bridged Events
nips.summary: Nostr events bridged from other protocols such as ActivityPub can link back to the source object by including a "proxy" tag, in the form:

nips.title: Private Key Encryption (ncryptsec)
nips.summary: This NIP defines a method by which clients can encrypt (and decrypt) a user's private key with a password.

nips.title: Search Capability
nips.summary: Many Nostr use cases require some form of general search feature, in addition to structured queries by tags or ids. Specifics of the search algorithms will differ between event kinds, this NIP only describes a general extensible framework for performing such queries.

nips.title: Lists
nips.summary: This NIP defines lists of things that users can create. Lists can contain references to anything, and these references can be public or private.
headings: A mute list with some public items and some encrypted items
A curation set of articles and notes about yaks
A release artifact set of an Example App

nips.title: Calendar Events
nips.summary: This specification defines calendar events representing an occurrence at a specific moment or between moments. These calendar events are addressable and deletable per NIP-09.

nips.title: Live Streaming and Spaces
nips.summary: This NIP introduces event kinds to advertise live spaces and the participation of pubkeys in them.

nips.title: Wiki
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:30818 (an addressable event) for descriptions (or encyclopedia entries) of particular subjects, and it's expected that multiple people will write articles about the exact same subjects, with either small variations or completely independent content.
headings: How to decide what article to display

nips.title: Android Signer Application
nips.summary: This NIP describes a method for 2-way communication between an Android signer and any Nostr client running on the same device, so that the client never needs to handle the user's private key. The signer is an Android application; the client may be another Android application or a web page.

nips.title: Reporting
nips.summary: A report is a kind 1984 event that signals to users and relays that some referenced content is objectionable. The definition of objectionable is obviously subjective and all agents on the network (users, apps, relays, etc.) may consume and take action on them as they see fit.

nips.title: Lightning Zaps
nips.summary: This NIP defines two new event types for recording lightning payments between users. 9734 is a zap request, representing a payer's request to a recipient's lightning wallet for an invoice.
headings: Appendix B: Zap Request HTTP Request
Appendix D: LNURL Server Zap Request Validation
Appendix G: zap tag on other events

nips.title: Badges
nips.summary: Four special events are used to define, award, display and categorize badges in user profiles:
headings: Example of a Badge Definition event
Example of a Profile Badges event

nips.title: Gift Wrap
nips.summary: This NIP defines a protocol for encapsulating any nostr event. This makes it possible to obscure most metadata for a given event, perform collaborative signing, and more.

nips.title: Static Websites (nsites)
nips.summary: This NIP describes a method by which static websites can be hosted from Blossom assets.

nips.title: Cashu Wallet
nips.summary: This NIP defines the operations of a cashu-based wallet.

nips.title: Nutzaps
nips.summary: A Nutzap is a P2PK Cashu token in which the payment itself is the receipt.

nips.title: Request to Vanish
nips.summary: This NIP offers a Nostr-native way to request a complete reset of a key's fingerprint on the web. This procedure is legally binding in some jurisdictions, and thus, supporters of this NIP should truly delete events from their database.

nips.title: Chess (PGN)
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:64 notes representing chess games in PGN format, which can be read by humans and is also supported by most chess software.

nips.title: Relay List Metadata
nips.summary: Defines a replaceable event using kind:10002 to advertise relays where the user generally writes to and relays where the user generally reads mentions.

nips.title: Relay Discovery and Liveness Monitoring
nips.summary: This NIP defines events for relay discovery and the announcement of relay monitors.

nips.title: EOSE Completeness Hint
nips.summary: This NIP extends the EOSE message defined in NIP-01 with an optional third element that signals the client that the relay has sent every stored event matching the subscription's filters.

nips.title: Picture-first feeds
nips.summary: This NIP defines event kind 20 for picture-first clients. Images must be self-contained. They are hosted externally and referenced using imeta tags.

nips.title: Peer-to-peer Order events
nips.summary: Peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms have seen an upturn in recent years, while having more and more options is positive, in the specific case of p2p, having several options contributes to the liquidity split, meaning sometimes there's not enough assets available for trading.

nips.title: Protected Events
nips.summary: When the "-" tag is present, that means the event is "protected".

nips.title: Video Events
nips.summary: This specification defines video events representing a dedicated post of externally hosted content.

nips.title: Moderated Communities
nips.summary: The goal of this NIP is to enable public communities. It defines the replaceable event kind:34550 to define the community and the current list of moderators/administrators. Users that want to post into the community, simply tag any Nostr event with the community's a tag.

nips.title: External Content IDs
nips.summary: There are certain established global content identifiers such as Book ISBNs, Podcast GUIDs, and Movie ISANs that are useful to reference in nostr events so that clients can query all the events associated with these ids.

nips.title: Zap Goals
nips.summary: This NIP defines an event for creating fundraising goals. Users can contribute funds towards the goal by zapping the goal event.

nips.title: Negentropy Syncing
nips.summary: This document describes a protocol extension for syncing events. It works for both client-relay and relay-relay scenarios. If both sides of the sync have events in common, then this protocol will use less bandwidth than transferring the full set of events (or even just their IDs).

nips.title: Application-specific data
nips.summary: The goal of this NIP is to enable remoteStorage-like capabilities for custom applications that do not care about interoperability.

nips.title: Forum Threads
nips.summary: A thread is a kind 11 event. Threads SHOULD include a title.

nips.title: Highlights
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:9802, a "highlight" event, to signal content a user finds valuable.

nips.title: Trusted Assertions
nips.summary: Certain Webs of Trust calculations require access to a large volume of events and/or computing power, making it virtually impossible to perform them directly on clients.

nips.title: Relay Management API
nips.summary: Relays may provide an API for performing management tasks. This is made available as a JSON-RPC-like request-response protocol over HTTP, on the same URI as the relay's websocket.

nips.title: Cashu and Fedimint Discoverability
nips.summary: This NIP describes kind:38173, kind:38172 and kind:38000: a way to discover ecash mints, their capabilities, and people who recommend them.

nips.title: Polls
nips.summary: This NIP defines the event scheme that describe Polls on nostr.

nips.title: Recommended Application Handlers
nips.summary: This NIP describes kind:31989 and kind:31990: a way to discover applications that can handle unknown event-kinds.
headings: User B interacts with a kind:31337-handler

nips.title: Data Vending Machines
nips.summary: This NIP defines the interaction between customers and Service Providers for performing on-demand computation.

unrecommended.reason: this got totally out of control, prefer use-case-specific microstandards

nips.title: Media Attachments Metadata (imeta)
nips.summary: Media attachments (images, videos, and other files) may be added to events by including a URL in the event content, along with a matching imeta tag.

nips.title: File Metadata
nips.summary: The purpose of this NIP is to allow an organization and classification of shared files. So that relays can filter and organize in any way that is of interest. With that, multiple types of filesharing clients can be created.

nips.title: HTTP File Storage Integration
nips.summary: This NIP defines a REST API for HTTP file storage servers intended to be used in conjunction with the nostr network. The API will enable nostr users to upload files and later reference them by url on nostr notes.
headings: List of Supporting File Storage Servers

nips.title: HTTP Auth
nips.summary: This NIP defines an ephemeral event used to authorize requests to HTTP servers using nostr events.

nips.title: Classified Listings
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:30402: an addressable event to describe classified listings that list any arbitrary product, service, or other thing for sale or offer and includes enough structured metadata to make them useful.

nips.title: Voice Messages
nips.summary: This NIP defines new events kind: 1222 for root messages and kind: 1244 for reply messages to be used for short voice messages, typically up to 60 seconds in length.

nips.title: payto: Payment Targets
nips.summary: This NIP standardizes how payment addresses are declared across any network or platform.

nips.title: Public Messages
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind 24 as a simple plaintext message to one or more Nostr users.

nips.title: Web Bookmarks
nips.summary: This NIP defines kind:39701 for a URI as editable web bookmark.

nips.title: Blossom
nips.summary: This NIP specifies how Nostr clients can use Blossom for handling media.

nips.title: Nostr BLE Communications Protocol
nips.summary: This NIP specifies how Nostr apps can use BLE to communicate and synchronize with each other. The BLE protocol follows a client-server pattern, so this NIP emulates the WS structure in a similar way, but with some adaptations to its limitations.

unrecommended.reason: only implemented once and unclear whether it works, requires review

nips.title: Code Snippets
nips.summary: This NIP defines a new event kind for sharing and storing code snippets. Unlike regular text notes (kind:1), code snippets have specialized metadata like language, extension, and other code-specific attributes that enhance discoverability, syntax highlighting, and improved user experience.

nips.title: Chats
nips.summary: A chat message is a kind 9 event.

nips.title: Geocaching
nips.summary: This NIP defines event kinds for geocaching on Nostr. These events allow users to create, share, and log geocaches in a decentralized manner.

nips.title: E2EE Messaging using MLS Protocol
nips.summary: This NIP standardizes how to use the MLS Protocol with Nostr for efficient and E2EE (end-to-end encrypted) direct and group messaging.

nips.title: Podcasts
nips.summary: This NIP defines how podcast episodes can be fetched from relays. It's intended to fit easily into existing podcast players.
